title: A morning in Johari Bazaar
excerpt: Pink arches, chai at 9 a.m., and the one lilac tray that became the Monsoon Hour jhumka.
author: Nemara Buying Team

body.text: We get to Johari Bazaar before ten, which in Jaipur means most shutters are still half down. That's the best time: owners have time to talk, and the trays haven't been picked over yet.
Red, green… and one tray of lilac

Almost every jhumka counter here leads with ruby red and emerald green. They're beautiful, and they're everywhere. Three shops in, we found a single tray of lilac meenakari — the enameller upstairs had been experimenting. That tray became our Monsoon Hour jhumka.
We asked for one change: a lighter dome, so you can wear them through a whole sangeet without your ears hating you. Two weeks later, the samples arrived.
Out of every fifty pieces we pick up in a market, one makes it to Nemara.
What we look for in Jaipur
Glossy enamel with no pinholes. Kundan that sits flush. Fringes that move. And colours that work with denim as much as with a lehenga.

title: How we check every piece before it reaches you
excerpt: Plating, stones, clasps, weight, edges — the checklist every Nemara find has to pass.
author: Nemara Quality Desk

cover.alt: Illustration of the Nemara checking table

body.text: Markets are where the magic is. They're also where quality varies the most. So nothing goes from a market tray straight into your bag — every piece comes through our checking table first.

Plating: checked under bright light for patches and bubbles. Stones and pearls: pushed, twisted and matched in pairs. Clasps and hooks: opened and closed until we trust them. Weight: earrings have to be comfortable for a full evening. Edges: every part that touches skin should feel smooth.
If a piece fails, it goes back. If a whole batch fails, we drop the design — however pretty it is.
Market finds, checked like fine jewellery. And backed by a 3-month warranty.
Then it's packed in a Nemara pouch with a card that tells you which market it came from — so your piece arrives with its story.

title: One kada, five versions of you
excerpt: The Ink & Gold pair, worn from a Monday stand-up to a Saturday sangeet.
author: Nemara Studio

cover.alt: Placeholder — kadas stacked on the wrist

body.text: Monday: one kada, crisp white shirt, sleeves pushed up. The purple line does the talking.
Wednesday: both kadas with a watch on the other wrist. Balanced, not matched.
Friday: stack them with the Recess bracelet. Play is allowed.
Saturday: with a silk saree and the Monsoon Hour jhumkas — gold to gold, lilac to purple.
Sunday: give one to your sister. She'll know why.
